item.title: East Providence's wild comeback ends 20 years of championship waiting
item.description: CRANSTON — Isaac Rodriguez guided East Providence 95 yards into the future. Rodriguez soaked in the Townies’ pride in their return to football glory as he glided down the left sideline at Cranston Stadium. He captained East Providence’s restoration with his winning interception in a game fitting for the super athlete. His final play — that unforgettable interception return — denied Burrillville as time expired in the Division II championship on Saturday afternoon. The Broncos pushed to win the game of the weekend, but Rodriguez smashed open East Providence’s trophy case for the first time since 2006. The 50-37 triumph on Nov. 21 is East Providence’s first football crown since that state championship victory against Hendricken and 16th title overall. The Townies are one of just two public schools to win a D-I title since that 2006 championship. “This is all of the East Providence right here,” Rodriguez said. “I got my friends. I got my family and my brothers right here. My coaches, anyone that believes in me is all right there. And my little role is just to show my love for them and for them being here and supporting the Townies.” The top-ranked Townies (8-0) and Burrillville combined for 36 points in the fourth quarter of a game that had five lead changes. Rodriguez hit Wynn Rabar for a 20-yard touchdown that gave East Providence a 44-37 lead with 1:09 left in regulation. Burrillville, playing in its first D-II championship, gained 45 yards in just under a minute to make a bid from the 21-yard line before Rodriguez dashed any hope. The quarterback managed five touchdowns in his MVP performance as East Providence rallied down 30-21 with less than a minute left in the third quarter. “Easily the craziest game I ever played in my life,” Rodriguez said. “I played basketball and track, I'm a three-sport athlete, but out of any sport I've ever played in my life, this is the craziest. I'm glad we were able to persevere, get through adversity, and get the job done.” “Thirty-six pass is the play call,” Rabar said. “I know that's my route. I'm the primary guy there. [Rodriguez] looked at me and I knew that was my ball to get to seal this game.” The Townies, after owning the late 90s and early 2000s, have had just seven winning seasons since 2006. It’s not where they should be, or where they want to be as one of the state’s biggest schools. Keeping their athletes in the district starts with Saturday’s win and continues with an eventual promotion to D-I. “I think that once the season starts next year, this doesn't matter anymore,” Xavier Rodriguez said. “But in this moment, celebrate as much as you can. item.description: ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 21: Savion Hiter #5 of the Michigan Wolverines runs the ball during the first quarter against Malik Hartford #12 of the UCLA Bruins at Michigan Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Jaime Crawford/Getty Images) | Getty Images It took a while, but Michigan pulled off the upset on Saturday and took down undefeated UCLA in overtime at the Big House by a final score of 18-16. It wasn’t perfect across the board, but here’s a look at the position grades from the win. Quarterback – C- Bryce Underwood made his first start for Michigan since he was benched against Penn State all the way back in Week 7. He didn’t look good last week against Oregon, but showed some improvement this week against UCLA, completing 11-of-24 passes for 127 yards and one touchdown. He also did have a fumble right before halftime, stalling out Michigan’s drive near midfield. Underwood didn’t do a great job throwing the ball downfield, overthrowing Travis Johnson on multiple occasions, but did look a bit more comfortable in the short-to-intermediate game, hitting the tight ends for some nice chunk plays. He saved his best throw for last, hitting Jalen Hoffman in the flat for the two-point conversion to win the game. He’ll likely start again next week, and probably gives Michigan the best chance to beat Ohio State. It was a solid but unspectacular day for Michigan’s freshman, who will hopefully play a big role next week against the Buckeyes. Travis Johnson did have an opportunity for a few big plays on the sideline, but was overthrown twice and had a pass interference not called against him in the first quarter. item.description: ‘This Is Awful,’ ‘So Terrible and Unnecessary’ — NFL Fans React to News of a Person’s Death Following Brawl at 49ers-Cowboys Game A Sunday afternoon at AT&T Stadium has turned into a death investigation for police in Arlington, Texas. Mario Narro, 36, fell during a fight with another fan around kickoff of the Dallas Cowboys’ November 15 game against the San Francisco 49ers, his family told police. Narro died three days later, but an official cause of death hasn’t been revealed. Word of his passing spread on Friday and drew a blunt response from NFL fans. Fans React to Mario Narro‘s Tragic Passing After Cowboys-49ers Fight Narro didn’t leave after the fall, his family said, and he was already hurting before the final whistle. Once the game ended, a friend who had come with Narro got the attention of paramedics inside the stadium, police said. The Tarrant County Medical Examiner’s Office said Narro died in intensive care at Medical City Arlington on Wednesday morning. How the fight started has not been made public. The friend reportedly did not see what happened during the altercation. Police have not released details about the other fan involved. Joe Schad, who covers the Miami Dolphins for the Palm Beach Post, tweeted: “We can’t have fans dying at games. This is terrible.” One fan had a similar reaction , calling the news “so terrible and unnecessary.” Another fan tweeted : “It’s a [expletive] football GAME!! It will never ever be that deep. This is awful.” “Just a reminder that the players and teams do not know of your existence as a fan,” another fan added. “I get supporting your squad but fighting over a team that can absolutely care less about you is wild to me.” “This [expletive] is so stupid. It’s a game at the end of the day,” commented another fan. item.title: NFL Punishes Two Players Over Cincinnati Bengals Game
item.description: The Bengals got bad news on two players after the win over the Steelers. Getty The NFL has taken disciplinary action against two Cincinnati Bengals players following the win over the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 10 on “Sunday Night Football,” namely Jordan Battle and Tedarrell Slaton. The decisions were expected for the Zac Taylor-led group. Per the NFL on November 21, Battle was fined $11,941 for “taunting.” It happened during the second quarter of the contest. On a second-and-10 from the Steelers 31, after Aaron Rodgers’ pass attempt to DK Metcalf fell incomplete, officials flagged Battle for the offense. Battle has contributed to the failed play for the Steelers, but his infraction gifted them 15 yards and a fresh set of downs. If Battle is flagged for taunting again, he could face a fine as high as $17,911. Bengals Get Good News Amid Fines for Jordan Battle, TJ Slaton After Steelers Game This is Battle’s second fine of the season. He received a $21,623 fine after Week 5 for unnecessary roughness over impermissible use of the helmet. This is Slaton’s first fine of the season. During the fourth quarter on a third-and-1 from Pittsburgh’s 41-yard line, Steelers running back Lew Nichols took a handoff for 3 yards. Kris Jenkins made the stop, but officials flagged Slaton for unnecessary roughness. The NFL announced on Saturday that it had fined Slaton $11,941 for a late hit, which opens him up to a $17,911 fine for a second offense. On a positive note, Jenkins avoided a fine. During the fourth quarter, officials flagged Jenkins for roughing the passer on a first-and-10 from the Bengals 44. Rodgers’ pass attempt to Germie Bernard had fallen incomplete on that play, too. Jenkins faced a fine that could reach $17,911. A second can incur a fine as high as $23,882. Steelers Avoid Bad More News After Bengals Game The Steelers came away from this contest scot-free in terms of additional discipline. They were not called for any infractions that were fineable during the game. However, the NFL’s decision not to fine Jenkins highlights a key aspect of the process. The NFL levies fines at its own discretion, leading to no fine for plays that were called and fines for ones that went uncalled. It can also lead to amounts that vary from what the NFL has officially listed. This time, though, the Steelers played a clean game in real time and upon further scrutiny from the league office. item.title: Texas Dominates Behind Another Impressive Performance From Arch Manning
item.description: Photo by: Scott Wachter The Texas Longhorns delivered a statement performance on Saturday, dominating Arkansas 45-3 at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Texas controlled the matchup from beginning to end, putting together an impressive performance on both sides of the football to earn its fifth consecutive victory. The No. 8 Longhorns entered the matchup knowing they needed to continue winning to keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive. With a difficult rivalry matchup against Texas A&M approaching, head coach Steve Sarkisian’s team took care of business against Arkansas. The victory improved Texas to 9-2 overall and 6-2 in SEC play, keeping the Longhorns firmly in the playoff conversation. Arch Manning Leads Texas Offensive Explosion Quarterback Arch Manning continued his impressive stretch of football, putting together another outstanding performance against Arkansas. Manning completed 21 of 25 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns while adding a rushing touchdown. His ability to make plays through the air and on the ground gave the Razorbacks defense problems throughout the afternoon. Texas wasted little time getting on the scoreboard. Manning capped the opening drive with a three yard touchdown run, giving the Longhorns an early 7-0 advantage. The Texas defense quickly added to the lead when Jelani McDonald intercepted an Arkansas pass and returned it 31 yards for a touchdown. McDonald’s interception return gave Texas a 14-0 advantage and immediately put Arkansas in a difficult position. The Longhorns continued building their lead during the second quarter. After adding a field goal, Manning connected with Emaree Winston for a 21 yard touchdown pass. Texas wasn’t finished before halftime. Manning found Emmett Mosley V for another touchdown, giving the Longhorns a commanding 31-3 advantage heading into the locker room. Arkansas struggled to generate explosive plays and couldn’t find the end zone throughout the afternoon. The Razorbacks also committed two turnovers, including McDonald’s interception return for a touchdown. Texas’ defense continued its dominance after halftime, holding Arkansas scoreless during the final two quarters. The Longhorns have now shown an impressive ability to close out games, allowing their opponents to struggle offensively late in contests. item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 21: Head coach Curt Cignetti of the Indiana Hoosiers looks on before the game against the Washington Huskies at Husky Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Indiana football dropped its first road game since 2024, falling 27-24 to Washington in overtime. Indiana’s defense stood tall to force a field goal from the Huskies in overtime, but Paddy McAteer saw his response kick blocked, ending the game in a shocking loss. Neither unit for Indiana, offense or defense, particularly shined today, but significant injuries to both sides made the result more predictable. The Hoosiers had overcome such a deficit against snake-bitten opponents like Nebraska and USC so far this year, but today, Washington brought too much. Overall, it was not a loss that is necessarily fatal, especially given the results ahead of Indiana in the rankings, but the on-field product was one that looked uncharacteristic for the Cignetti era, evoking memories of the Hoosiers’ past. item.title: No. 5 Texas routs Arkansas to all but lock up berth in College Football Playoff
item.description: In what might've been Arch Manning's final regular-season home game with Texas, he directed a blowout of Arkansas to all but put Texas in the College Football Playoff. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) AUSTIN - Fifth-ranked Texas all but secured its spot in the upcoming College Football Playoff by crushing Arkansas 45-3 on Saturday afternoon at Royal-Memorial Stadium for its fifth consecutive win. The Longhorns completed their regular-season home schedule before 102,508 on Senior Day when 38 Texas players were honored. That number included fourth-year quarterback Arch Manning, who had one of his finest performances in what could be his final home game at DKR although he has another year of eligibility remaining if he chooses to take it. In the first half alone, Manning completed 15 of 17 passes for 230 yards and two touchdowns and ran for another score and led Texas to a 31-3 halftime bulge. The two touchdown passes to tight end Emaree Winston and wide receiver Emmett Mosley V came in the final 2 minutes and 20 seconds of the second quarter. Manning finished with 287 yards on 21-of-25 passing before exiting after the third quarter. He has compiled a 21-5 record as a starter with nine of those wins coming in 11 games against Top 25 teams. Sophomore backup KJ Lacey came on, connected with transfer receiver Sterling Berkhalter on a brilliant 35-yard play before handing off to freshman Derrek Cooper on an 8-yard touchdown run to complete the scoring. Texas scored on five of its first six offensive series, four of them touchdowns, and six of its eight possessions in the game. Arkansas found its way into Longhorn territory six times in the game, but produced a lone 30-yard field goal by Max Gilbert. The Razorbacks missed a field goal and gave up the ball on misfired fourth-down tries. Arkansas managed 363 yards of offense but became Texas' fourth straight opponent to fail to score a single point in the fourth quarter. The Longhorns allowed the visitors just 135 yards after intermission. The Longhorns, who were ranked fifth in the most recent CFP rankings and might well move up, improved their record to 9-2 with the regular-season finale against archrival Texas A&M on Friday night in College Station. Texas sits at 6-2 in conference play trails league leader Georgia by one game in the SEC standings. Arkansas, which was coming off a huge upset of South Carolina, fell to 4-7 and 2-6 in conference action. item.description: Well, that was not how Penn State' s last home game of the season should have gone. Against a quarterback with cracked ribs on a 2-8 team, you would think that the Nittany Lions would have coasted to a win. Think again. They ultimately blew a 14-point second-half lead and lost on a last-second two-point conversion against Rutgers . While there were solid performances on the day, they felt anomalous in a stunning loss that probably won't sit well with the fans of this team for a long time. Both Chase Sowell and Tony Rojas deserve a ton of respect for playing through the ineptitude and are deserving of the players of the game for this week. It just feels weird that they didn't come in a win. Offense: Chase Sowell It is utterly crazy that when Penn State finally finds a star receiver, they fail to find talent around him to supplement his level of play. That seems to be the case with Chase Sowell this season. The Iowa State transfer has had to step up due to Koby Howard's injury and yet has received little support from the offense around him. His 123 yards and a touchdown kind of feel like a fever dream now simply because you could say he was the only source of offense for much of this game for the blue and white. If that weren't the case, we would probably be singing his praises in a more well-rounded team victory. Now, we're left to wonder what Sowell would look like in a more competent offense. Defense: Tony Rojas Tony Rojas probably has it worse than any other Penn State player. He actually spent all of his college career in Happy Valley through many highs and lows. He has seen the College Football Playoff and has seen a bad .500 season. And yet, his level of play never drops, no matter the team around him. Unfortunately for him, the team around him has been in decline ever since his sophomore season. A player with 14 tackles and 1.5 TFLs should be lauded as a superstar. Tony Rojas almost certainly is. The only problem is that he's one for a pretty average team. Follow Nittany Lions Wire on X and Facebook . item.description: The San Antonio Spurs hosted their third annual Champions for Change fundraiser Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, at the Victory Capital Performance Center, bringing together players, coaches, franchise legends and community members to raise more than $1.1 million for programs at the Spurs Impact Center. (Isaiah Alonzo) The San Antonio Spurs brought together their full roster, franchise legends and team executives Friday night for a record-breaking fundraiser that raised more than $1.1 million for community programs across San Antonio. The third annual Champions for Change event, presented by Meter, welcomed about 500 guests to the Victory Capital Performance Center on Nov. 20 for an evening of basketball-inspired entertainment, art and exclusive experiences with Spurs players. All Spurs players attended, along with head coach Mitch Johnson and franchise legends George Gervin, David Robinson and Sean Elliott. Spurs Sports & Entertainment CEO R.C. Buford and members of the Holt family also attended. The amount raised exceeded the organization's expectations and surpassed its $1 million fundraising goal, according to Patricia Mejia, chief impact and inclusion officer for Spurs Sports & Entertainment. "Absolute shock," Mejia said in an interview with the Express-News. "This is a record-breaking number." The money will support programming at the Spurs Impact Center, a $10 million transformation of the team's former practice facility into a community hub focused on youth sports, leadership development and workforce readiness. For Spurs forward Keldon Johnson, the fundraiser carried personal significance because the Impact Center occupies the same building where he spent the early years of his NBA career. "It's a blessing to be able to be a part of something like this," Johnson said. "Being able to give back to the Impact Center, somewhere that I started my career at, where I put a lot of blood, sweat and tears into being over there, it means the world to me." Johnson said the former practice facility holds countless memories from his development as a young player, making its transformation into a community resource particularly meaningful. "That's where I got my first opportunity to be a professional," Johnson said. Mejia said the organization wants to use basketball to introduce young people to opportunities beyond the court, including science, technology and career development. One upcoming program, Basketball and Tech, will teach participants about the science and mathematics behind basketball, including career opportunities in the sport that don't involve playing. The center also works to make youth sports more accessible to families who might otherwise struggle with the rising costs of participation. Other initiatives include leadership training for nonprofit organizations and workforce development partnerships. item.description: Credit: OutKick Plenty of football fans have tired of seeing Kirk Herbstreit trot out his golden retriever, but Craig Carton might have pushed that annoyance a bit too far. item.description: The defending national champions are in position to miss the College Football Playoff entirely. No. 8 Indiana made a quarterback change back to Josh Hoover but still lost 27-24 to Washington in overtime , giving the Hoosiers a second Big Ten loss and giving them only a slim chance of returning to the conference championship game. With the loss, Indiana drops into a tie for second place in the conference with Oregon and Iowa . Unfortunately for the Hoosiers, they lose the tiebreaker to both teams and would have just one path to the title game: beating Purdue while the Hawkeyes lose to Nebraska and the Ducks to the Huskies . The playoff selection committee has already made its feelings on Indiana known. The Hoosiers debuted at No. 4 in this year's rankings but dropped five spots to No. 9 one week later after needing overtime to beat Minnesota. While they rebounded to No. 8 after beating No. 19 Southern California, the Hoosiers are clearly not a darling of the committee and could drop out of the top 12 on Tuesday night. That perception won't be changed by a win against Purdue. It’s been a tough year for a team that basically cruised to last year’s national title. After failing to give even a loose approximation of Fernando Mendoza’s impact in 2025, Hoover is the face of the Hoosiers’ weekly struggle to even reach this point. Since beating Rutgers 47-15 in early October, Indiana has scored more than 24 points in a game just once, in last week’s 27-13 win against Southern California. The wins against the Scarlet Knights and Trojans are its only Big Ten games decided by double-digit margins. Still, the Hoosiers could’ve overcome their relatively anemic strength of schedule and lack of marquee wins by continuing to win ugly. After a miserable run of heartbreaking losses against No. 8 Indiana, No. 14 Oregon and Washington, Nebraska won the fourth quarter and beat No. 17 Ohio State 31-28 to snap the program’s 31-game winless streak against ranked competition. This is an exhale moment for coach Matt Rhule, who has seen his decision to replace Dana Holgorsen as offensive coordinator pay off with back-to-back wins. Defensively, the Cornhuskers were down multiple key contributors but held the Buckeyes to just 335 yards of offense and forced two turnovers. item.description: For the first time this season, the Chicago Blackhawks (7-14-2) won a game that wasn’t played at the United Center, defeating the Calgary Flames (10-12-2) 4-3 in overtime at Scotiabank Saddledome on Saturday. Sam Rinzel continued his scorching-hot stretch, scoring the overtime winner and adding two assists for his fifth straight multi-point performance. Rinzel became the first Blackhawks defenseman with five consecutive multi-point games since Pierre Pilote in 1962. Rinzel has been nothing short of terrific recently, but he played perhaps his best NHL game on Saturday. The 22-year-old chipped in on three of the team’s four goals and also made a game-saving play in the final minute of regulation, using his stick to prevent Flames forward Matt Coronato from burying a wrap-around game-winner. In 22 games this season, Rinzel already has a career-high 15 points and 17 assists. He’s only one point behind captain Connor Bedard for the team lead in points. Patrick Kane also played his best game of the season in Calgary, snapping his career-long 18-game goal drought and adding two assists in 19:26 of ice time. It was Kane’s first three-point outing since returning to the Blackhawks. Without Bedard, the Blackhawks need “Showtime” to step up, and he certainly did that on Saturday. Kane, who turned 38 earlier this week, recorded a game-high 11 shot attempts, eight individual scoring chances, and seven shots on goal, along with his three points. Roman Kantserov and Ryan Donato also scored for the Blackhawks, with the former becoming the first NHL rookie to reach 10 goals this season. Kantserov added an assist on Rinzel’s game-winning goal and has now recorded a point in six straight road games. Spencer Knight had a shaky outing in Thursday’s loss to the Columbus Blue Jackets, but he rebounded nicely and was an unsung hero against Calgary, stopping 33 of 36 shots. Ryan Strome, Jonathan Castagna, and Yegor Sharangovich (PP) scored for Calgary, while Dustin Wolf allowed four goals on 33 shots. The Blackhawks had to overcome plenty of adversity on Saturday to earn their first road win and second in eight games without Bedard this season. item.title: Texas Tech's postseason path becomes clear, with CFP wrinkles thrown in
item.description: Just as the Texas Tech football team kicked things off with Baylor in Waco, another game up in the Sunflower State kept my attention a big longer. BYU and Kansas were headed to overtime, the game as important for the Red Raiders as Tech's was against the Bears. A loss by the Cougars meant Texas Tech just needed to win in McLane Stadium to clinch a return trip to the Big 12 Conference championship. Alas, the Jayhawks couldn't get the job done, falling in triple-overtime. That didn't matter much, since Tech still needed to beat Baylor for anything else to matter elsewhere. Then a sequence of events after Tech's 20-10 win over Baylor opened the door even more. Sure, Joey McGuire's team is right where it was at the start of the weekend, needing to win out to return to Arlington. That didn't change. Texas Tech will have to earn its way to Jerry World on Thanksgiving Day against TCU in Galaxy Stadium. The path to the Big 12 title game is clear. The question that's come around Lubbock land as of late is whether the Red Raiders can get to the College Football Playoff without a repeat performance there. Seemed far-fetched to think the Big 12 would get the benefit of having multiple teams in the CFP unless one of them was BYU by virtue of its win over Notre Dame. The Cougars, however, haven't looked great since that game and can count themselves lucky to leave Lawrence with the dub. No, the Big 12's ultimate fate rested elsewhere, namely the Big Ten and SEC. Those two conferences are always going to trump the Big 12 and ACC when it comes to the CFP. To get Utah and another team into the field, Brett Yormark's soon-to-be-former conference was going to need chaos to happen elsewhere. Minutes after Tech wrapped up its win over Baylor, Indiana lost 27-24 in overtime on the road at Washington. Reigning national champs or not, the CFP committee clearly hasn't thought too highly of the Hoosiers' resume to this point, which, admittedly, looks weak on paper. Good, close losses are only allowed in the SEC, whether Curt Cignetti likes it or not. Then another domino fell when UCLA lost in triple-overtime at Michigan. With so few undefeated teams left in the country, the Bruins have risen up to top-five status in recent weeks. But like Indiana, a closer look at UCLA's resume — i.e. the teams its actually beaten — is less than stellar. UCLA was fourth in last week's CFP rankings, Indiana eighth. Combined, those two teams have two wins over teams in the CFP's recent Top 25: UCLA defeated Oregon (a team that lost to Oklahoma State, a team Texas Tech decimated) while Indiana has defeated USC. Texas Tech, which was 12th, has wins over two CFP teams itself, having topped Arizona and Houston. These points will surely get brought up over the next few days, and will be the center of the conversation come Tuesday night when another non-sensical version of the CFP rankings drops. There's no telling if UCLA and Indiana losing will help the Red Raiders move up the rankings or not.

item.title: Lions Starter Punished for Actions in Blowout Win Over Patriots
item.description: One Detroit Lions player was fined but he NFL for his actions against the New England Patriots Getty Detroit Lions CB Rock Ya-Sin was fined but he NFL for what he did against the Patriots Getty New England Patriots QB Drake Maye was injured on a third-down sack against the Lions Getty The New England Patriots flew home from Munich with a 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions and a starting quarterback who may not play again this season. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye left on the opening drive with what ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported was a fractured ankle that could keep him out for the rest of the year. It was the second straight blowout for New England. The Patriots (5-5) have now lost three of their last four games. Though the Lions celebrated the win, it came at a cost for one of their players on Saturday. Lions CB Disciplined for Aggressive Play vs. Patriots Getty Detroit Lions CB Rock Ya-Sin was fined but he NFL for what he did against the Patriots The NFL fined Lions cornerback Rock Ya-Sin $11,941 for unnecessary roughness (facemask) in the third quarter, according to the league’s weekly game day accountability report . By then, the Lions already led 28-3. However, the Patriots were finally moving the ball. Late in the third quarter, New England put together its best drive since Maye went down. A.J. Brown sparked it with a 22-yard catch-and-run, then stayed down holding his right leg and left with a hamstring injury. Ya-Sin got the better of Brown earlier in the game too. Brown couldn’t shake free from the veteran CB on one Tommy DeVito throw that sailed through his hands. Ya-Sin was only in the lineup because Lions CB1 D.J. Reed couldn’t play. item.description: Cowboys star CeeDee Lamb received the NFL's largest fine of the week following the 49ers game. Here's what prompted the punishment and why it stands out. Getty Dallas Cowboys receiver CeeDee Lamb was fined $23,882 by the NFL for illegal use of the helmet on a block in the Nov. 15 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. But despite being hit with the largest punishment of the week, in terms of fines handed down for actions on the field, Lamb was not penalized by game officials for the alleged transgression. The flag that flew on the play never counted. Officials picked it up, the touchdown stood, and a league review after the fact turned a non-call into a five-figure bill. Lamb says his helmet never touched the defender. So what did the NFL see on the replay? Read More From Heavy What’s Up With the Cowboys’ Injuries? Lamb cleared the way against 49ers cornerback Deommodore Lenoir with a shoulder block that left him airborne . The league ruled that Lamb’s helmet made contact with Lenoir. Lamb confirmed Thursday that helmet contact was the reason for the fine, though he denies it happened and said the rest of the conversation could wait for another day, according to the Dallas Sports Journal . He has also said the threat of fines makes him pull back from blocking. Was a penalty called on the field? Sort of. Officials threw a flag, then picked it up without enforcing a penalty , and the official gamebook lists no accepted or declined foul on Lamb, according to the Journal . item.title: Lakers rookie makes most of biggest opportunity he’s gotten so far
item.description: Lakers coach JJ Redick has emphasized for weeks that every player on his roster is going to get an opportunity to play. The nature of an 82-game regular season necessitates flexibility with playing rotations. Cameron Carr of the Los Angeles Lakers drives to the basket. NBAE via Getty Images During Friday’s 106-104 home win over the Kings , rookie Cameron Carr got his most significant opportunity with the Lakers to date. And his performance showed why he’s deserving of more playing opportunities moving forward. With Austin Reaves sidelined for the fourth consecutive game because of a bruised left heel, Carr was in the rotation off the bench, playing 11 minutes. Unlike some of his previous playing time, a good amount of which has come when the game’s results were already decided, the former Baylor Bear’s minutes had a direct impact on the Lakers’ chances of winning. And the rookie made the playing time count, having five points on 2-for-5 shooting (1-for-4 on 3-pointers), a steal and a rebound. “He looked great,” Walker Kessler said. “He hit some big shots, played with physicality. He’s got some long arms, I can tell you that. That layup he made — he’s just got some long arms. He looked good tonight. I was happy. It was good to see.” Cameron Carr of the Los Angeles Lakers speaks to the media. NBAE via Getty Images The stats don’t matter as much as the comfort Carr showed when he was on the court. He didn’t hesitate to shoot the corner 3-pointer that momentarily gave the Lakers a two-point lead midway through the second quarter. And didn’t shy away from contact on a layup later in the quarter. Carr looked ready for the defensive physicality needed to hold his own on that end of the floor. “That was huge,” Quentin Grimes said. “I mean, as a rookie, you got to go out there and kind of earn minutes. Everybody kind of has to do that at one point some time in their career. And he got thrown in there, hit a big 3, hit a tough layup and had a couple good closeouts and got some stops. So, those are the things that earn trust from a coach when they throw you out there even more later in the season, for sure.” Redick has said Carr and second-year forward Adou Thiero’s development over the next couple of years could raise the team’s collective ceiling. But before they can be ceiling-raisers, Carr and Thiero need to establish a floor for themselves. Jaden Hardy #7 and Cameron Carr #43 of the Los Angeles Lakers smile during a game against the Sacramento Kings. NBAE via Getty Images Friday was a step in that direction. More opportunities will come for Carr. With Reaves expected to make his return to the floor next week, playing time won’t be available as it has been with him sidelined. But Carr showed, at least for one game, he’s ready to contribute more when his number is called. And it’s on the Lakers to find more chances for him so he can develop into the ceiling-raiser they’re looking for him to be.

item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
